Map the provided canvas’s diagram nodes to the source-code line ranges that explain or implement them.

For each node, select the source ranges that together explain what the node represents. Read the label in the context of its branch. A single-line leaf can stand for an entire subsystem. Use the following rules to decide when you have enough evidence.

- For a specific fact, stop when the source establishes it. A declaration listing all allowed states can fully support a node that simply names those states.
- For a subsystem, identify its principal responsibilities in the pinned source and follow its entry point to where those responsibilities are implemented. For a compound label, check each named behavior, resource, or ownership claim. A field declaration can establish who holds a resource. If the label also describes its lifetime, find where the owner acquires, transfers, or releases it, as applicable.
- For a flow, follow the handoffs in the label. Select the code that connects the steps and performs the named transformations. A caller that delegates the work may be a useful first jump. Follow the call to the implementation when the label describes what that work does.

Keep each range tight. Use several disjoint ranges in one file or across files when the evidence is distributed. Choose ranges for the node itself, using its parent and children to clarify scope. A parent does not need the union of every descendant’s mappings, and a child may need direct evidence beyond its parent’s range.

Before validating, review each node against its selected lines. Could a reader verify each material claim from those lines? Follow any missing claim into the source. If only part is supported, keep the verified ranges and identify the diagram, node, and unresolved claim in notes. If no part is supported, leave the node unmapped and explain why in notes. Carry every verified range into the complete candidate and final submission.

Register the mappings, preserving every diagram’s content and the canvas layout.

Inputs and submission: the saved AgentContext contains the pinned repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). Use the available read/bash tools to inspect that checkout. Use the supplied diagrams as-is. No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Return only JSON: {"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Any unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}. Include every supplied diagram, using an empty mappings array if needed. Each entry maps one supplied node reference to one repository-relative, 1-based inclusive source range; repeat the node for multiple ranges. Do not change diagram text or layout.

The runner registers these exact node/range choices through the setSourceMappings operation underlying nodes.setSourceMappings. It resolves the supplied node references to their current diagram spans and fills evidence.originalLines from the pinned source. It does not choose, widen or repair source ranges. The checkout is read-only; no canvas tools are exposed inside this evaluation session.

Before submission, read each selected range with line numbers that restart for that file (for example, nl -ba one-file.ts). Do not infer range endpoints from search hits or use cumulative numbering across files. Call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate JSON, inspect any reported errors, and verify corrected ranges against the source before returning the final JSON. The final JSON must match a candidate that passed this check. This tool checks node references, file existence and line bounds; semantic support still requires your inspection. Validation calls and any within-session corrections are retained as part of the same sample; they are not separate generation attempts.

   272	/// Drain the mailbox.
   273	fn drainMailbox(self: *App, rt_app: *apprt.App) !void {
   274	    while (self.mailbox.pop(global.io())) |message| {
   275	        if (comptime std.log.logEnabled(.debug, .app)) {
   276	            switch (message) {
   277	                // these tend to be way too verbose for normal debugging
   278	                else => log.debug("mailbox message={t}", .{message}),
   279	            }
   280	        }
   281	        switch (message) {
   282	            .open_config => |v| try self.performAction(
   283	                rt_app,
   284	                .{
   285	                    .open_config = switch (v) {
   286	                        .os_open => .os_open,
   287	                        .new_window => .new_window,
   288	                    },
   289	                },
   290	            ),
   291	            .new_window => |msg| try self.newWindow(rt_app, msg),
   292	            .close => |surface| self.closeSurface(surface),
   293	            .surface_message => |msg| try self.surfaceMessage(msg.surface, msg.message),
   294	
   295	            // If we're quitting, then we set the quit flag and stop
   296	            // draining the mailbox immediately. This lets us defer
   297	            // mailbox processing to the next tick so that the apprt
   298	            // can try to quit as quickly as possible.
   299	            .quit => {
   300	                log.info("quit message received, short circuiting mailbox drain", .{});
   301	                try self.performAction(rt_app, .quit);
   302	                return;
   303	            },
   304	        }
   305	    }

   831	    if (self.search) |*s| s.deinit();
   832	
   833	    // Stop rendering thread
   834	    {
   835	        self.renderer_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   836	            log.err("error notifying renderer thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   837	        self.renderer_thr.join();
   838	    }
   839	
   840	    // Stop our IO thread
   841	    {
   842	        self.io_thread.stop.notify() catch |err|
   843	            log.err("error notifying io thread to stop, may stall err={}", .{err});
   844	        self.io_thr.join();
   845	    }
   846	
   847	    // We need to deinit AFTER everything is stopped, since there are
   848	    // shared values between the two threads.
   849	    //
   850	    // The renderer must be deinitialized before the renderer thread:
   851	    // on macOS the renderer's display link callback points at the
   852	    // thread's `draw_now` handle, and the renderer's deinit is what
   853	    // stops the display link for good.
   854	    self.renderer.deinit();
   855	    self.renderer_thread.deinit();
   856	    self.io_thread.deinit();
   857	    self.mouse.selection_gesture.deinit(&self.io.terminal);
   858	    self.io.deinit();

   860	    if (self.inspector) |v| {
   861	        v.deinit(self.alloc);
   862	        self.alloc.destroy(v);
   863	    }
   864

   866	    for (self.keyboard.sequence_queued.items) |req| req.deinit();
   867	    self.keyboard.sequence_queued.deinit(self.alloc);
   868	    self.keyboard.table_stack.deinit(self.alloc);
   869	
   870	    // Clean up our font grid
   871	    self.app.font_grid_set.deref(self.font_grid_key);

   873	    // Clean up our render state
   874	    if (self.renderer_state.preedit) |p| self.alloc.free(p.codepoints);

    78	/// Create a new app instance. This returns a stable pointer to the app
    79	/// instance which is required for callbacks.
    80	pub fn create(alloc: Allocator) CreateError!*App {
    81	    var app = try alloc.create(App);
    82	    errdefer alloc.destroy(app);
    83	    try app.init(alloc);
    84	
    85	    // If font discovery supports warmup, then we call it. Some font
    86	    // mechanisms (e.g. CoreText) have a multi-millisecond one-time cost
    87	    // on startup.
    88	    if (comptime @hasDecl(font.Discover, "warmup")) {
    89	        if (std.Thread.spawn(
    90	            .{},
    91	            font.Discover.warmup,
    92	            .{},
    93	        )) |thr| thr.detach() else |err| {
    94	            log.warn("font warmup thread spawn failed err={}", .{err});
    95	        }
    96	    }
    97	
    98	    // Same for the renderer's graphics API (e.g. Metal), which pays
    99	    // one-time framework initialization costs on first use.
   100	    if (comptime @hasDecl(renderer.Device, "warmup")) {
   101	        if (std.Thread.spawn(
   102	            .{},
   103	            renderer.Device.warmup,
   104	            .{},
   105	        )) |thr| thr.detach() else |err| {
   106	            log.warn("renderer warmup thread spawn failed err={}", .{err});
   107	        }
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    return app;
   111	}

   220	/// Delete the surface from the known surface list. This will NOT call the
   221	/// destructor or free the memory.
   222	pub fn deleteSurface(self: *App, rt_surface: *apprt.Surface) void {
   223	    // If this surface is the focused surface then we need to clear it.
   224	    // There was a bug where we relied on hasSurface to return false and
   225	    // just let focused surface be but the allocator was reusing addresses
   226	    // after free and giving false positives, so we must clear it.
   227	    if (self.focused_surface) |focused| {
   228	        if (focused == rt_surface.core()) {
   229	            self.focused_surface = null;
   230	        }
   231	    }
   232	
   233	    var i: usize = 0;
   234	    while (i < self.surfaces.items.len) {
   235	        if (self.surfaces.items[i] == rt_surface) {
   236	            _ = self.surfaces.swapRemove(i);
   237	            continue;
   238	        }
   239	
   240	        i += 1;
   241	    }
   242	
   243	    // If we have no surfaces, we can start the quit timer. It is up to the
   244	    // apprt to determine if this is necessary.
   245	    if (self.surfaces.items.len == 0) _ = rt_surface.rtApp().performAction(
   246	        .app,
   247	        .quit_timer,
   248	        .start,
   249	    ) catch |err| {
   250	        log.warn("error starting quit timer err={}", .{err});
   251	    };
   252	}

   273	fn drainMailbox(self: *App, rt_app: *apprt.App) !void {
   274	    while (self.mailbox.pop(global.io())) |message| {
   275	        if (comptime std.log.logEnabled(.debug, .app)) {
   276	            switch (message) {
   277	                // these tend to be way too verbose for normal debugging
   278	                else => log.debug("mailbox message={t}", .{message}),
   279	            }
   280	        }
   281	        switch (message) {
   282	            .open_config => |v| try self.performAction(
   283	                rt_app,
   284	                .{
   285	                    .open_config = switch (v) {
   286	                        .os_open => .os_open,
   287	                        .new_window => .new_window,
   288	                    },
   289	                },
   290	            ),
   291	            .new_window => |msg| try self.newWindow(rt_app, msg),
   292	            .close => |surface| self.closeSurface(surface),
   293	            .surface_message => |msg| try self.surfaceMessage(msg.surface, msg.message),
   294	
   295	            // If we're quitting, then we set the quit flag and stop
   296	            // draining the mailbox immediately. This lets us defer
   297	            // mailbox processing to the next tick so that the apprt
   298	            // can try to quit as quickly as possible.
   299	            .quit => {
   300	                log.info("quit message received, short circuiting mailbox drain", .{});
   301	                try self.performAction(rt_app, .quit);
   302	                return;
   303	            },
   304	        }
